quests.hint: This verb means to act as a neutral party helping two groups reach an agreement.
quests.explanation: 'Mediate a dispute,' 'mediate between,' and 'skilled mediator' are key. 'Mediation' is the noun. 'Mediator' is the person. Used in legal, business, and diplomatic contexts.
quests.textToSpeak: The HR manager had to ___ between the two team members to resolve the conflict.
quests.correctAnswer: The HR manager had to mediate between the two team members to resolve the conflict.

quests.hint: This verb means to help make a meeting or process run smoothly and productively.
quests.explanation: 'Facilitate a meeting,' 'facilitate discussion,' and 'facilitator' are key. 'Facilitation' is the noun. Facilitating is different from leading - you guide rather than direct.
quests.textToSpeak: She was asked to ___ the workshop and ensure all voices were heard equally.
quests.correctAnswer: She was asked to facilitate the workshop and ensure all voices were heard equally.

quests.hint: This verb means to expect or predict something before it actually happens.
quests.explanation: 'Anticipate problems,' 'anticipate demand,' and 'fail to anticipate' are key. 'Anticipation' is the noun: 'in anticipation of.' Good managers are praised for anticipating challenges.
quests.textToSpeak: A good leader learns to ___ potential problems before they become serious issues.
quests.correctAnswer: A good leader learns to anticipate potential problems before they become serious issues.

quests.hint: This verb means to identify something as important and deal with it appropriately.
quests.explanation: 'Address a problem,' 'address the issue,' and 'address the audience' are key. 'Address' can also mean where someone lives. 'Address concerns' is very common in professional English.
quests.textToSpeak: The manager agreed to ___ all the concerns raised at the next team meeting.
quests.correctAnswer: The manager agreed to address all the concerns raised at the next team meeting.

quests.hint: This verb means to officially start or introduce a new product, service, or campaign.
quests.explanation: 'Launch a product,' 'launch a campaign,' and 'product launch' are key. 'Launch' can be a noun: 'the launch of a new range.' 'Soft launch' means a limited initial release.
quests.textToSpeak: The company plans to ___ the new product range across Europe next spring.
quests.correctAnswer: The company plans to launch the new product range across Europe next spring.

quests.hint: This verb means to set up and put something into a stable, working condition.
quests.explanation: 'Establish a business,' 'establish a routine,' and 'well-established' are key. 'Establishment' is the noun. 'Long-established' means it has existed for a long time.
quests.textToSpeak: It took her two years to ___ the company as a respected name in the industry.
quests.correctAnswer: It took her two years to establish the company as a respected name in the industry.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a central idea or message that runs throughout a text or discussion.
quests.explanation: 'Main theme,' 'recurring theme,' and 'explore a theme' are key. 'Thematic' is the adjective. 'Common theme' means a subject that appears repeatedly across different works.
quests.textToSpeak: The central ___ of the novel is the struggle between personal freedom and duty.
quests.correctAnswer: The central theme of the novel is the struggle between personal freedom and duty.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a temporary mental picture or image that represents something abstract.
quests.explanation: 'Create an image,' 'paint an image,' and 'vivid imagery' are key. 'Imagery' (collective noun) refers to a collection of vivid descriptions in a literary text.
quests.textToSpeak: Her writing creates powerful ___ of rural life that stays with the reader for days.
quests.correctAnswer: Her writing creates powerful imagery of rural life that stays with the reader for days.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the main character or lead figure of a story or situation.
quests.explanation: 'The protagonist faces,' 'a flawed protagonist,' and 'sympathetic protagonist' are key. The opposite is 'antagonist' - the character who opposes the protagonist.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ of the novel is a young woman who must choose between love and ambition.
quests.correctAnswer: The protagonist of the novel is a young woman who must choose between love and ambition.

quests.hint: This adjective describes a claim or idea that has not yet been fully proved or verified.
quests.explanation: 'Tentative conclusion,' 'tentative agreement,' and 'tentatively suggest' are key. 'Tentatively' is the adverb. A tentative plan is one that might change. It implies caution.
quests.textToSpeak: She offered a ___ conclusion based on the early data, pending further research.
quests.correctAnswer: She offered a tentative conclusion based on the early data, pending further research.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the meaning or importance attached to words or actions beyond the literal.
quests.explanation: 'Symbolic significance,' 'of great significance,' and 'historical significance' are key. 'Significant' and 'significantly' are related forms. 'Without significance' means unimportant.
quests.textToSpeak: The date of the speech was chosen because of its great historical ___.
quests.correctAnswer: The date of the speech was chosen because of its great historical significance.

quests.hint: This verb means to show or demonstrate something clearly through evidence or action.
quests.explanation: 'Demonstrate skills,' 'demonstrate understanding,' and 'clearly demonstrate' are key. 'Demonstration' is the noun. 'Demonstrate' is more formal than 'show.'
quests.textToSpeak: She was able to ___ her expertise through the quality of her written work.
quests.correctAnswer: She was able to demonstrate her expertise through the quality of her written work.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a basic element or quality that something cannot function without.
quests.explanation: 'Essential skill,' 'absolutely essential,' and 'it is essential that' are key. 'Essentials' (plural) refers to the most basic things needed. 'Non-essential' means optional.
quests.textToSpeak: Good communication skills are ___ for anyone working in a client-facing role.
quests.correctAnswer: Good communication skills are essential for anyone working in a client-facing role.

quests.hint: This adjective describes a plan or option that is practical and likely to succeed.
quests.explanation: 'Viable option,' 'viable alternative,' and 'commercially viable' are key. 'Viability' is the noun: 'assess the viability.' 'Not viable' means unlikely to work or succeed.
quests.textToSpeak: The committee reviewed the proposals and selected the most ___ option available.
quests.correctAnswer: The committee reviewed the proposals and selected the most viable option available.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that is broad, complete, and covers every aspect.
quests.explanation: 'Comprehensive report,' 'comprehensive review,' and 'comprehensive knowledge' are key. 'Comprehensively' is the adverb. More formal than 'full' or 'complete.'
quests.textToSpeak: She prepared a ___ report covering every aspect of the project's performance.
quests.correctAnswer: She prepared a comprehensive report covering every aspect of the project's performance.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the reasons or logic that supports or justifies a decision.
quests.explanation: 'The rationale behind,' 'explain the rationale,' and 'provide a rationale' are key. More formal than 'reason.' 'Rationale' is often used in academic and professional writing.
quests.textToSpeak: She was asked to explain the ___ behind her decision to restructure the team.
quests.correctAnswer: She was asked to explain the rationale behind her decision to restructure the team.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that relates to evidence gathered through direct observation.
quests.explanation: 'Empirical evidence,' 'empirical research,' and 'empirically tested' are key. 'Empirical' contrasts with 'theoretical.' 'Empirically supported' means backed by observable data.
quests.textToSpeak: The theory is supported by solid ___ evidence collected over many years.
quests.correctAnswer: The theory is supported by solid empirical evidence collected over many years.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the method or set of methods used to conduct a study or research.
quests.explanation: 'Research methodology,' 'qualitative methodology,' and 'justify your methodology' are key. 'Methodical' is a related adjective meaning systematic and careful.
quests.textToSpeak: The examiner asked her to explain and justify the ___ she used in her research.
quests.correctAnswer: The examiner asked her to explain and justify the methodology she used in her research.

quests.hint: This noun refers to what a text or speaker implies but does not state directly.
quests.explanation: 'Read the subtext,' 'underlying subtext,' and 'political subtext' are key. 'Subtext' is what lies beneath the surface meaning. Very important in literature and communication analysis.
quests.textToSpeak: What makes the speech so powerful is the clear ___ of threat beneath the polite words.
quests.correctAnswer: What makes the speech so powerful is the clear subtext of threat beneath the polite words.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the underlying structure of a society, organisation, or system.
quests.explanation: 'Critical infrastructure,' 'transport infrastructure,' and 'invest in infrastructure' are key. 'Infrastructural' is a formal adjective. Roads, power grids, and internet are all infrastructure.
quests.textToSpeak: Without adequate digital ___, many rural communities cannot access online services.
quests.correctAnswer: Without adequate digital infrastructure, many rural communities cannot access online services.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a fundamentally different way of thinking about or approaching a subject.
quests.explanation: 'Paradigm shift,' 'established paradigm,' and 'challenge a paradigm' are key. Kuhn used 'paradigm shift' to describe scientific revolutions. A widely used academic term.
quests.textToSpeak: Artificial intelligence represents a genuine ___ shift in how we work and communicate.
quests.correctAnswer: Artificial intelligence represents a genuine paradigm shift in how we work and communicate.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the wider effect or meaning something has beyond its immediate context.
quests.explanation: 'Broader implications,' 'political implications,' and 'have serious implications' are key. 'Implication' can also mean an indirect suggestion. 'By implication' means indirectly.
quests.textToSpeak: This finding has significant ___ for how we approach early childhood education.
quests.correctAnswer: This finding has significant implications for how we approach early childhood education.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that is deeply embedded and part of the essential nature.
quests.explanation: 'Intrinsic value,' 'intrinsic motivation,' and 'intrinsically linked' are key. 'Extrinsic' is the opposite - coming from outside. 'Intrinsic reward' comes from within the task itself.
quests.textToSpeak: Learning a language has ___ value beyond its practical career benefits.
quests.correctAnswer: Learning a language has intrinsic value beyond its practical career benefits.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something clear and well-expressed, with ideas flowing logically.
quests.explanation: 'Coherent argument,' 'coherent explanation,' and 'lack of coherence' are key. 'Coherently' is the adverb. 'Incoherent' means confused or impossible to follow.
quests.textToSpeak: The essay presented a highly ___ argument that was easy to follow from start to finish.
quests.correctAnswer: The essay presented a highly coherent argument that was easy to follow from start to finish.

quests.hint: This adjective describes a statement that could mean more than one thing - not clear.
quests.explanation: 'Deliberately ambiguous,' 'deliberately vague,' and 'remove ambiguity' are key. 'Ambiguity' is the noun. 'Ambiguous phrasing' is a common problem in contracts and instructions.
quests.textToSpeak: The contract contained deliberately ___ wording that caused confusion on both sides.
quests.correctAnswer: The contract contained deliberately ambiguous wording that caused confusion on both sides.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something subtle, with small but important differences in meaning.
quests.explanation: 'Nuanced argument,' 'nuanced understanding,' and 'highly nuanced' are key. 'Nuance' is the noun. 'Lacking nuance' means treating complex things too simply.
quests.textToSpeak: Her ___ analysis acknowledged that the situation was far more complex than it appeared.
quests.correctAnswer: Her nuanced analysis acknowledged that the situation was far more complex than it appeared.

quests.hint: This adjective describes an idea so deeply felt or profound it reaches the core of thinking.
quests.explanation: 'Profound impact,' 'profound insight,' 'a profound truth,' and 'profoundly changed' are key. 'Profound' is stronger than 'deep.' 'Profoundly' is the adverb: 'profoundly affected.'
quests.textToSpeak: Reading that book had a truly ___ effect on how she thought about her own life.
quests.correctAnswer: Reading that book had a truly profound effect on how she thought about her own life.

quests.hint: This adjective describes language that is used to persuade an audience effectively.
quests.explanation: 'Rhetorical question,' 'rhetorical device,' and 'powerful rhetoric' are key. 'Rhetoric' is the art of effective speech. 'Rhetorical' can imply that no answer is expected.
quests.textToSpeak: He used a number of ___ devices to make his closing argument more persuasive.
quests.correctAnswer: He used a number of rhetorical devices to make his closing argument more persuasive.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a comparison made between two things to explain or clarify an idea.
quests.explanation: 'Draw an analogy,' 'by analogy,' and 'useful analogy' are key. An analogy explains something unfamiliar by comparing it to something familiar. Widely used in teaching.
quests.textToSpeak: She used an ___ to a river and its banks to explain the concept of boundaries.
quests.correctAnswer: She used an analogy to a river and its banks to explain the concept of boundaries.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the effect a piece of writing, speech, or action has on the reader.
quests.explanation: 'Emotional impact,' 'make an impact,' 'have a significant impact,' and 'lasting impact' are key. 'Impactful' is an adjective. 'High-impact' describes something very effective.
quests.textToSpeak: The simplicity of the final paragraph gave the essay tremendous ___.
quests.correctAnswer: The simplicity of the final paragraph gave the essay tremendous impact.
